use: Heard in announcements and travel plans; in conversation 'arrive' is usually tsuku.

example.ja: 飛行機の到着、遅れるって。
example.english: They say the plane's going to be late.

examplePolite.romaji: hikouki no touchaku ga okureru sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 飛行機の到着が遅れるそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear the plane's arrival is delayed.

notes: As a verb, touchaku suru sounds formal: mamonaku touchaku shimasu (we'll arrive shortly).

use: Movement toward the speaker; you going along with someone is tsuite iku.

example.ja: 道分かるから、ついてきて。
example.english: I know the way, follow me.

examplePolite.romaji: michi ga wakarimasu kara, tsuite kite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 道が分かりますから、ついてきてください。
examplePolite.english: I know the way, so please follow me.

notes: Also 'comes with' for extras: omake ga tsuite kuru (it comes with a freebie).

english: move (from one place to another), get from A to B
use: Going somewhere else, on foot or by transport; not moving house (hikkosu) or budging (ugoku).

example.ja: そろそろ移動しようか。
example.english: Shall we move on?

examplePolite.romaji: sorosoro idou shimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: そろそろ移動しましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we head over soon?

notes: idouchuu = on the way, in transit (common in texts).

english: show around, guide; show the way

example.ja: この辺、案内するよ。
example.english: I'll show you around the area.

examplePolite.romaji: kono hen o annai shimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: この辺を案内しますよ。
examplePolite.english: I'll show you around the area.

notes: Staff say goannai shimasu (let me show you). annaijo = information desk.

use: For people; coming to collect a thing is tori ni kuru.

example.romaji: eki made mukae ni kite kureru?
example.ja: 駅まで迎えに来てくれる？
example.english: Can you come pick me up at the station?

examplePolite.romaji: eki made mukae ni kite moraemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 駅まで迎えに来てもらえますか？
examplePolite.english: Could you come and pick me up at the station?

notes: Going to pick someone up is mukae ni iku.

example.ja: 何時に出発する？
example.english: What time are we leaving?

examplePolite.romaji: nanji ni shuppatsu shimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何時に出発しますか？
examplePolite.english: What time do we leave?

notes: shuppatsu! on its own = off we go! In casual talk, deru often does the same job.

example.romaji: kaeri wa watashi ga unten suru yo.
example.ja: 帰りは私が運転するよ。
example.english: I'll drive on the way back.

examplePolite.romaji: kaeri wa watashi ga unten shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 帰りは私が運転します。
examplePolite.english: I'll drive on the way back.

notes: unten menkyo = driver's licence; unten miawase = trains not running.

english: go along with, follow; keep up
use: Movement away from the speaker: you go with someone.

example.ja: 私もついていっていい？
example.english: Can I come along too?

examplePolite.romaji: watashi mo tsuite itte mo ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 私もついていってもいいですか？
examplePolite.english: May I come along too?

notes: tsuite ikenai = can't keep up (with a class or the pace).

use: The corner takes o, the direction ni: kado o migi ni magaru.

example.romaji: tsugi no kado, migi ni magatte.
example.ja: 次の角、右に曲がって。
example.english: Turn right at the next corner.

examplePolite.romaji: tsugi no kado o migi ni magatte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 次の角を右に曲がってください。
examplePolite.english: Please turn right at the next corner.

notes: Also for things bent or crooked: nekutai magatteru yo (your tie's crooked).

use: Toward the speaker or the place being talked about.

example.ja: 今度彼女連れてきてよ。
example.english: Bring your girlfriend next time.

examplePolite.romaji: kondo kanojo-san mo tsurete kite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 今度彼女さんも連れてきてください。
examplePolite.english: Please bring your girlfriend next time too.

notes: Bringing a thing is motte kuru, not tsurete kuru.

use: Away from the speaker; tsurete itte! = take me with you!

example.romaji: kodomo, byouin ni tsurete iku ne.
example.ja: 子ども、病院に連れて行くね。
example.english: I'll take our kid to the doctor.

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo o byouin ni tsurete ikimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 子どもを病院に連れて行きます。
examplePolite.english: I'm taking my child to the doctor.

notes: Taking a thing is motte iku. Often shortened to tsureteku.

use: Usually as konde iru / konderu (is crowded).

example.ja: 今日、電車すごい混んでるね。
example.english: The train's really packed today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa densha ga totemo konde imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は電車がとても混んでいますね。
examplePolite.english: The train's very crowded today.

use: The line you switch to takes ni.

example.ja: 新宿で乗り換えるよ。
example.english: We change at Shinjuku.

examplePolite.romaji: shinjuku de norikaemasu.
examplePolite.ja: 新宿で乗り換えます。
examplePolite.english: We change trains at Shinjuku.

notes: norikae = a transfer. Also used casually for switching phones or partners.

use: Laughing at someone takes o: hito o warau.

example.romaji: chotto, warawanaide yo! shinken nan dakara.
example.ja: ちょっと、笑わないでよ！真剣なんだから。
example.english: Hey, don't laugh! I'm serious.

examplePolite.romaji: warawanaide kudasai. shinken nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: 笑わないでください。真剣なんです。
examplePolite.english: Please don't laugh. I'm serious.

notes: Covers smiling too: waratte! = smile! (for photos).

english: rest, take a break; take time off (school, work)
use: Skipping school or work takes o: gakkou o yasumu.

example.romaji: netsu aru kara, kyou gakkou yasumu.
example.ja: 熱あるから、今日学校休む。
example.english: I've got a fever, so I'm skipping school today.

examplePolite.romaji: netsu ga aru node, kyou wa yasumimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 熱があるので、今日は休みます。
examplePolite.english: I have a fever, so I'll take today off.

notes: oyasumi = good night; chotto yasumou = let's take a break.

use: For people collapsing, often from illness, and things toppling over.

example.ja: お父さんが倒れたって！
example.english: Dad's collapsed!

examplePolite.romaji: chichi ga taoreta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 父が倒れたんです。
examplePolite.english: My father has collapsed.

notes: Tripping while walking is korobu; taoreru is more serious.

use: The 'look down on' sense is common in arguments: namenna yo! (don't mess with me).

example.romaji: aite o namenai hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: 相手をなめない方がいいよ。
example.english: Better not underestimate them.

examplePolite.romaji: aite o namenai hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 相手をなめない方がいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You shouldn't underestimate them.

notes: The lick sense is everyday too: aisu o nameru (lick an ice cream), ame o nameru (suck a candy).

example.ja: カラオケで何歌う？
example.english: What are you going to sing at karaoke?

examplePolite.romaji: karaoke de nani o utaimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: カラオケで何を歌いますか？
examplePolite.english: What will you sing at karaoke?

use: Actually being asleep; going to bed is neru.

example.ja: 夕べは暑くて全然眠れなかった。
example.english: It was so hot I couldn't sleep at all last night.

examplePolite.romaji: yuube wa atsukute zenzen nemuremasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 夕べは暑くて全然眠れませんでした。
examplePolite.english: It was so hot I couldn't sleep at all last night.

notes: nemui = sleepy. nemurenai (can't sleep) is the form you'll hear most.

english: get hungry (stomach); empty out, get less crowded
use: Mostly onaka ga suita (I'm hungry) and suite iru (not crowded).

example.ja: ああ、お腹すいた！なんか食べよう。
example.english: Ugh, I'm starving! Let's eat something.

examplePolite.romaji: onaka ga sukimashita ne. nanika tabemashou.
examplePolite.ja: お腹がすきましたね。何か食べましょう。
examplePolite.english: I'm getting hungry. Let's eat something.

notes: The same kanji read aku means 'become free': seki ga aita (a seat opened up).
